## Design

### 2026-10-18 – I designed and built this custom enclosure for my "Starbie" companion robot completely from scratch

**5h**

I designed and built this custom enclosure for my "Starbie" companion robot completely from scratch
i was inspired by a yeti model online so i used it and modified ir based on my needs and i will make many changes after my 3d model is printed manully .

After setting up the main body shells to properly house my ESP32 board, battery, and internal wiring, I mapped out and carved a custom 22mm x 11mm window right in the front to create a clean, flush fit for my 0.96-inch OLED screen i changed many more thing like adding many required things .

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 231621](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EMj7OOJJEoRobI2cOU9tmZbKMZE2QmsM/7ab7eafe4685a16376bb41efb1c84bca42b3db99989b178a36fbddd1b7eb9c7f.png)

Instead of keeping everything as one single piece, I kept the front face plate separate from the main body. This lets me export them individually so I can 3D print the face plate in a totally different color than the body, giving it a cool multi-color look before gluing everything together.

### 2026-10-18 – I designed and built this custom enclosure for my "Starbie" companion robot completely from scratch in Tinkercad.

**6h**

I designed and built this custom enclosure for my "Starbie" companion robot completely from scratch in Tinkercad.

After setting up the main body shells to properly house my ESP32 board, battery, and internal wiring, I mapped out and carved a custom 22mm x 11mm window right in the front to create a clean, flush fit for my 0.96-inch OLED screen.

Instead of keeping everything as one single piece, I kept the front face plate separate from the main body. This lets me export them individually so I can 3D print the face plate in a totally different color than the body, giving it a cool multi-color look before gluing everything together.
